title: The Computable (Recursive) Symmetric Group on ℕ
description: A child result of OQ-03 (Myhill's isomorphism theorem, the computable analogue of Schröder–Bernstein). Isolates and fully verifies the structural fact the priority construction implicitly rests on: the computable permutations of ℕ — bijections e with both e and e.symm Computable — form a subgroup recSym of the symmetric group Equiv.Perm ℕ, the classical recursive symmetric group. Every transposition Equiv.swap m n is computable (via an explicit Primrec witness), so the subgroup generated by all transpositions is computable and every finite product of transpositions — hence every finitely-supported permutation of ℕ — is computable. The group is nontrivial. Fully machine-checked, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext:
Myhill's isomorphism theorem (1955) is the computable refinement of the Cantor–Schröder–Bernstein theorem: two predicates with computable one-one reductions in both directions are related by a computable permutation of ℕ. Its proof (Rogers, Theory of Recursive Functions, §7.4) is a back-and-forth priority construction that chains finitely many computable adjustments at each stage and must remain computable throughout. The parent entry `schroeder-bernstein-oq-03` builds the full infrastructure for this construction; the hard direction — the priority argument itself — is still open there.

The object that makes 'chaining computable adjustments stays computable' precise is the group of computable permutations of ℕ, classically called the recursive symmetric group. This entry isolates that object and verifies it is a genuine subgroup, together with its most basic generators.
overview.proofStrategy:
1. **Transposition computability (Section 1)**: `primrec_swapFun` witnesses the swap function as an `ite`-tree over `PrimrecRel.comp Primrec.eq …` equality tests; `Primrec.to_comp` and `Computable.of_eq` (rewriting by `Equiv.swap_apply_def`) give `computable_swap_coe`; `Equiv.symm_swap` then yields `swap_computable`.

2. **The subgroup (Section 2)**: `recSym` is assembled field-by-field. `one_mem'` rewrites `Equiv.Perm.one_def` and discharges both coordinates with `Computable.id` after `Equiv.coe_refl`/`Equiv.refl_symm`. `mul_mem'` rewrites `Equiv.Perm.mul_def` and applies `Equiv.Computable.trans`; `inv_mem'` rewrites `Equiv.Perm.inv_def` and applies `Equiv.Computable.symm`.

3. **Generators and structure (Section 3)**: `swap_mem` is `swap_computable`; `closure_isSwap_le` uses `Subgroup.closure_le` with an `rintro ⟨x, y, -, rfl⟩` on `IsSwap`; `list_prod_swap_mem` uses `Subgroup.list_prod_mem`; `recSym_ne_bot` derives a contradiction from `swap 0 1 = 1` by evaluating both sides at 0 (`Equiv.swap_apply_left`, `Equiv.Perm.coe_one`).
keyInsights: **Composition-closure is the reusable core of any effective back-and-forth.** The reason a stage-wise priority construction can adjust the partial bijection finitely often and still yield a *computable* total permutation is exactly that computable permutations are closed under composition and inverse — the subgroup structure abstracts that closure away from the specific construction.

**Transpositions are the computable generators.** A single decidable-equality `ite` makes each swap primitive recursive, and self-inverseness makes the inverse free. From these, closure under the group operations propagates computability to the entire transposition-generated subgroup with no further computability arguments.

**Finitely-supported ⟹ computable, for free.** Because every finitely-supported permutation of ℕ is a finite product of transpositions, `list_prod_swap_mem` gives their computability immediately from the subgroup laws — no separate encoding of the support is needed.

**Group membership is classical, not decidable.** `recSym` is an ordinary `Subgroup`: `e ∈ recSym` is the *proposition* `e.Computable`. The entry does not (and cannot, in general) claim this membership is decidable — only that the computable permutations are closed under the group operations.

sections.title: Transpositions are Computable
sections.summary: primrec_swapFun witnesses the swap function x ↦ if x = m then n else if x = n then m else x as primitive recursive; computable_swap_coe transfers it to Equiv.swap via swap_apply_def; swap_computable adds self-inverseness (symm_swap) to get (Equiv.swap m n).Computable.
sections.mathContext: The transposition function is an ite-tree over decidable equality tests, hence Primrec, hence Computable; a swap equals its own inverse, so both computability halves of Equiv.Computable coincide.

sections.title: The Recursive Symmetric Group
sections.summary: recSym : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm ℕ) with carrier {e | e.Computable}; one_mem'/mul_mem'/inv_mem' discharged via Equiv.Perm.one_def / mul_def / inv_def together with Computable.id and Equiv.Computable.trans / .symm. mem_recSym records that membership is definitionally e.Computable.
sections.mathContext: Identity id is computable and 1.symm = 1; a * b = b.trans a and composition of computable equivs is computable; a⁻¹ = a.symm and inverse of a computable equiv is computable.

sections.title: Generators and Structure
sections.summary: swap_mem places every transposition in recSym; closure_isSwap_le contains the transposition-generated subgroup in recSym; computable_of_mem_closure_isSwap and list_prod_swap_mem expose computability of arbitrary transposition products (hence all finitely-supported permutations); recSym_ne_bot shows the group is nontrivial.
sections.mathContext: The subgroup generated by { σ | σ.IsSwap } lies inside recSym; every finite product of swaps is computable; swap 0 1 ≠ 1 witnesses recSym ≠ ⊥.

conclusion.summary: We isolate and fully verify the group-theoretic backbone of OQ-03's computable back-and-forth: the computable permutations of ℕ form a subgroup recSym of the symmetric group Equiv.Perm ℕ — the recursive symmetric group. Every transposition is computable via an explicit Primrec witness, so the transposition-generated subgroup is computable and every finitely-supported permutation of ℕ is computable; the group is nontrivial. All results are machine-checked with 0 sorries and 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications:
**A reusable abstraction for effective bijection-building.** Any back-and-forth or priority construction that adjusts a partial bijection through finitely many computable steps stays computable precisely because recSym is closed under composition and inverse; this entry makes that closure a first-class, verified object rather than an inline argument.

**Generators handled once.** Reducing computability of finitely-supported permutations to computability of a single transposition means later work in the OQ-03 family can invoke swap_mem / list_prod_swap_mem instead of re-deriving computability of concrete permutations.
openQuestions: Is membership e ∈ recSym decidable relative to an index for e — i.e. can one give an effective (index-level) presentation of the recursive symmetric group, quantifying its arithmetical complexity?

Extend closure_isSwap_le to a full characterization: is every finitely-supported permutation's computability exactly captured by the transposition closure, and how does recSym sit between the finitely-supported permutations and all of Equiv.Perm ℕ?
Complete the parent's hard direction (the Myhill priority construction) using recSym as the target group for the stage-wise computable adjustments.
